executive_summary: Replace a DISSOLVED coupling with the invariant that actually protects the hazard, and delete the one that no longer can. FR-3's count-visibility coupling guarded against a rate limit STARVED by a narrow SELECT policy. That failure mode is now impossible: the counted set moved inside fn_anon_ingress_prior_hour_count, which is SECURITY DEFINER and postgres-owned, so the count is RLS-independent. PROVEN BEHAVIOURALLY, not argued — as anon, row_security_active(feedback)=TRUE and a direct count returns 0, while the SAME anon calling the definer function receives 8, the owner's true count. THE HAZARD DID NOT VANISH, IT RELOCATED into whether that count still ignores the caller's visibility. So the new invariant asserts THE OUTCOME, not the mechanism: as anon, the definer count must EQUAL the owner's true count. A FLAG CAN BE GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON; A BEHAVIOURAL EQUALITY CANNOT — which is why the originally-ruled two-flag check was refuted and superseded before any code was written.

functional_requirements.title: Assert the behavioural equality inside the ALREADY-ARMED probe, not in a new instrument
functional_requirements.description: Extend assertIngressBoundCannotBind in scripts/anon-write-contract-probe.mjs. It is ALREADY ARMED on a daily cron, ALREADY does `set local role anon` with comparative counts inside a savepoint, and ALREADY computes definerFnBasis from the policy body — roughly 90% of the correct invariant already exists there. Adding a third comparator to the divergence fence instead would graft a function/table-posture check onto a script whose identity is 'two separately-editable objects that must agree', and would leave the probe's existing basis logic duplicated. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE IS NAMED SO IT IS NOT RE-PROPOSED: lib/policy/anon-chairman-boundary.js declares security_definer and even carries feedback_force_row_security as INHERITED_UNVERIFIED, but its object is record_venture_error — a DIFFERENT function — and its probe scripts/probe-anon-chairman-reach.mjs is fully dormant. Extending an armed instrument is the 1-REP move the parent SD made.

functional_requirements.title: THE ASSERTION MUST REACH THE EXIT CODE — it is print-only otherwise
functional_requirements.description: MEASURED AT LEAD AND IT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WITHOUT THIS REQUIREMENT. probeTable:446 assigns the bound result only when !control, :447 swallows throws into a note, :463 sets res.bound, and main():522-530 merely PRINTS it — while main():532 folds ONLY r.code into the running worst exit code, and r.code comes from compare(res.observed) at :462/:467 alone. NO FIELD OF res.bound EVER REACHES THE EXIT CODE. So a perfectly correct equality added inside assertIngressBoundCannotBind would change nothing observable: a detector nobody reads, for the THIRD time in this arc. probeTable and main must fold the new verdict into the exit code, and probeTable is NOT exported — so the acceptance has to prove the fold, not just the assertion.

functional_requirements.title: The invariant is a PAIR, not a single equality — and prosecdef demotes to a diagnostic
functional_requirements.description: THE EQUALITY ALONE IS SATISFIED BY A GLOBALLY-INERT RLS, which is this probe's own most-guarded failure (documented at :26-33). So the invariant is BOTH halves: (anon-observed definer count EQUALS the owner's true count) AND (anon's DIRECT count is LESS THAN the owner's true count). The first half proves the definer still ignores caller visibility; the second half proves RLS is genuinely in force, so the first half means something. The negative control already exists in the function — asAnon.n at :347 is the anon direct count. Note assertIngressBoundCannotBind, unlike runForms:266, never calls assertRlsInForce, which is exactly why the second half must be explicit here. AGREES iff both hold. This is MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC and therefore immune in ONE check to all four ways the hazard returns: (1) DOMINANT — ALTER FUNCTION OWNER TO a role that is neither the table owner nor BYPASSRLS-holding, after which RLS applies to the definer and the measured anon-direct 0 is what it would count, so `0 < 50` is unconditionally true and the limit never binds; (2) the function BODY is rewritten (narrower WHERE, different interval, different relation); (3) the policy RE-INLINES the count, running as the inserting role, with the function untouched; (4) REVOKE EXECUTE from anon — PRECEDENTED HERE by 20260603_03, which revoked anon EXECUTE from ~112 SECDEF functions on 2026-06-03, BEFORE this function existed, and which fails CLOSED (ingress outage) rather than starving. prosecdef is still READ and REPORTED as a diagnostic that explains a failure, but it is NOT the pass condition. Reporting a posture flag as the verdict is what made the superseded design wrong.

functional_requirements.title: relforcerowsecurity MUST NOT be a pass condition — it is a proven false-positive term
functional_requirements.description: STATED AS A REQUIREMENT BECAUSE IT WAS THE RULED DESIGN AND WOULD OTHERWISE BE RE-ADDED BY ANY REASONABLE READER. postgres holds rolbypassrls=TRUE, and BYPASSRLS is checked BEFORE the owner/FORCE test, so setting FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on feedback would NOT resurrect the hazard. Proven by NATURAL EXPERIMENT on live production with ZERO DDL: ai_gen_provenance and ai_gen_dwell_tracking both have relforcerowsecurity=TRUE and are postgres-owned, yet row_security_active() returns FALSE for postgres on both. A check keyed on that flag would DIVERGE ON A HARMLESS FLIP — the wolf-cry in a new costume, i.e. precisely the defect this SD exists to remove. It may be recorded as context; it may never gate the verdict.

functional_requirements.title: RETIRE compareCountVisibility outright, and record WHY on the way out
functional_requirements.description: Unwire it from the fence (sole runtime caller scripts/severity-pair-divergence-fence.mjs:296, import :50) and DELETE it, its tests, and the then-dead module-private extractLimitPredicate at fence:89. The contingency is satisfied: it was the only thing positioned to notice an inline-count regression, and FR-2's behavioural equality covers that path. LEAVE-IN-PLACE-UNUSED IS EXPLICITLY REJECTED — an exported comparator with nine green tests, one of them titled 'AGREES today', is a lie waiting for a reader who greps it and concludes a live guard protects the count. The dissolution AND refutation citations must land in the module docstring: deleting silently is exactly the 'coupling vanishes without a record' this SD's binding condition forbids, and FR-3 is another SD's RATIFIED acceptance criterion. Note fence:305 emits `count` in the --json payload, so the machine-readable surface changes too, not only the human one.

functional_requirements.title: Carry the dissolution and refutation citations onto the record
functional_requirements.description: Binding condition (B). The SD description was amended BEFORE this PRD (the SD-edits-after-PRD-never-reach-EXEC trap is live), and the probe's comment contract must carry the same two citations: the pg_get_functiondef readback plus the three posture facts, AND the refutation of the two-flag remedy with its natural-experiment proof. A future reader must be able to see WHY the original coupling retired and WHY the obvious replacement was rejected — otherwise the two-flag design gets re-proposed on first principles.

technical_requirements.title: Catalog reads must be signature-qualified
technical_requirements.description: Use ::regprocedure, never a bare `where proname='fn_anon_ingress_prior_hour_count'`. One row exists today, but an overload silently returns two and any not-a-boolean/row-picking rule then depends on undefined ordering. The same discipline applies to the relation: qualify to public.

technical_requirements.title: Read-only. No DDL, no policy or grant mutation, in any framing
technical_requirements.description: Instrument-only: it reads catalog and executes a STABLE counting function inside a transaction it does not commit. The probe's existing savepoint discipline is preserved. 'Inside a rolled-back transaction to test it' is not an exemption for DDL and none is needed here.

technical_requirements.title: An unreadable basis must never report AGREES
technical_requirements.description: If either side of the equality cannot be obtained, the result is UNREADABLE — not a pass. This is the module-wide design rule the parent instrument already encodes, and it is the difference between 'the counts matched' and 'I could not compare them'.

technical_requirements.title: The acceptance is a PROBE-LEVEL assertion, not a live posture proof — say so
technical_requirements.description: There is no non-production database and the flags live in the live catalog, so the two-sided proof runs at the probe's own testable surface with constructed inputs. That is the strongest DDL-free form available; the PRD says it plainly rather than letting the acceptance read as a live production proof it is not.

test_scenarios.scenario: POSITIVE CONTROL — the equality HOLDS on today's real posture
test_scenarios.expected: anon-observed definer count EQUALS the owner's true count (the measured 8 == 8) and the check AGREES. Without this, an implementation that failed on every path would satisfy every negative case while alarming forever.

When the anon-observed count differs from the owner's true count (the shape every one of the four hazard paths produces), the check reports DIVERGED and names the two counts. Binding condition (A), fire half.

test_scenarios.scenario: NEGATIVE CONTROL — the harmless FORCE-RLS flip stays SILENT
test_scenarios.expected: A posture with relforcerowsecurity=TRUE on a postgres-owned table does NOT fire, because BYPASSRLS is checked first and the equality still holds. THE FALSE POSITIVE CAUGHT DURING LEAD BECOMES THE CONTROL THAT PROVES IT WAS REMOVED — modelled on the ai_gen_provenance / ai_gen_dwell_tracking natural experiment. Binding condition (A), silent half. A build that kept the flag as a pass condition fails HERE.

test_scenarios.scenario: SEEDED — an INERT RLS does NOT pass, even though the equality holds
test_scenarios.expected: With anon_via_fn === owner_count but anon_direct === owner_count (RLS not actually in force), the check does NOT agree. This is the hole in the single-equality design: a globally-bypassed RLS satisfies the equality while the contract is void. A build asserting only the equality passes every other scenario and fails HERE.

test_scenarios.scenario: SEEDED — an unreadable basis is UNREADABLE, never AGREES
test_scenarios.expected: A missing or non-numeric count on either side yields UNREADABLE. An implementation that treats an unobtained count as 'equal' reports a healthy contract it never measured.

test_scenarios.scenario: THE VERDICT REACHES THE EXIT CODE — not merely the console
test_scenarios.expected: A DIVERGED bound verdict makes main() return a non-zero code. Asserted through the exported main() with an injected q, because res.bound currently reaches only console.log while the exit code folds r.code alone. A build that adds a correct assertion without folding it in passes every scenario above while remaining incapable of failing — the exact defect this SD family exists to kill.

test_scenarios.scenario: The retired comparator is GONE, not merely unwired
test_scenarios.expected: compareCountVisibility and extractLimitPredicate are absent from the codebase, and the fence's results array and --json payload no longer reference `count`. An exported-but-uncalled comparator with green tests is the failure this scenario exists to prevent.

test_scenarios.scenario: The citations survive in the module contract
test_scenarios.expected: The probe's comment contract carries both the dissolution citation and the refutation of the two-flag remedy. Asserted so a later tidy-up cannot quietly remove the only explanation of why this check looks the way it does.

acceptance_criteria: The behavioural invariant is asserted inside the already-armed anon-write-contract probe — no new instrument, no third comparator in the fence.
THE VERDICT REACHES THE EXIT CODE. A DIVERGED bound result makes main() return non-zero — proven, not assumed. An assertion that only prints is the defect, not the fix.
The invariant is the PAIR (definer count equals owner's true count AND anon's direct count is less than it) — an inert RLS must not pass on the equality alone.
The check FIRES on a constructed basis-divergence and stays SILENT on the harmless FORCE-RLS flip; both directions mutation-proven, not one and an assumption.
relforcerowsecurity is nowhere a pass condition; prosecdef appears only as a diagnostic.
compareCountVisibility, its tests, and the dead extractLimitPredicate are DELETED, and the fence's --json payload no longer emits `count`.
The dissolution and refutation citations are on the SD record and in the probe's comment contract.

SCOPED DELIBERATELY TO THE FR-3 COUPLING ALONE: the fence's parity coupling is GENUINELY DIVERGED (v_patterns_with_decay is missing six columns present on issue_patterns). That is real debt owned by the parent SD's remit and is EXCLUDED-WITH-REASON here — so the fence still exiting 1 after this SD lands is the KNOWN divergence, not this SD's failure. Any criterion expecting the fence to go green would be unachievable by construction.

risks.risk: The two-flag design is re-proposed on first principles, because it is the obvious one and it was once ruled.
risks.mitigation: FR-3 states the prohibition AS A REQUIREMENT with its natural-experiment proof, and TS-3 fails any build that reinstates it. The refutation is on the SD record and in the module contract.

risks.risk: compareCountVisibility is left exported-but-unused as the 'safe' option.
risks.mitigation: FR-4 and TS-5. It is the WORST option: nine green tests including one titled 'AGREES today' would tell a future reader a live guard exists where none does.

risks.risk: The check is built to assert prosecdef because a flag is easier to read than a behaviour.
risks.mitigation: FR-2 demotes it explicitly and TS-2/TS-3 are keyed on the equality. A flag can be green for the wrong reason — that sentence is the whole design.

risks.risk: Someone reads the acceptance as a live production proof.
risks.mitigation: TR-4 states the venue plainly. Overstating what a test proves is how a bounded claim becomes an unstated assumption.

risks.risk: The fence still exits 1 after this lands, and a reader concludes the SD failed.
risks.mitigation: The excluded-with-reason acceptance criterion names the parity divergence and its owner.

integration_operationalization.consumers: The daily anon-write-contract probe workflow, and anyone asking whether the anon ingress rate limit still binds. Downstream: SD-LEO-INFRA-THREE-GAPS-APPLIED-001, whose FR-3 acceptance criterion this retires-with-citation rather than silently drops.
integration_operationalization.dependencies: scripts/anon-write-contract-probe.mjs (assertIngressBoundCannotBind — the host, already armed); scripts/severity-pair-divergence-fence.mjs (unwire the retired coupling); lib/policy/severity-pair-coupling.js (delete the comparator, carry the citation); the live catalog via the probe's existing pg connection.
integration_operationalization.data_contracts: No schema changes. Reads pg_proc/pg_class and executes a STABLE counting function inside the probe's existing savepoint. Mutates nothing.
integration_operationalization.runtime_config: None new — the host probe is already scheduled and already holds its credentials. That is the point of choosing it.
integration_operationalization.observability_rollout: Before: FR-3 reports UNREADABLE against a coupling that no longer exists, and no instrument watches the hazard's new location. After: one behavioural equality inside an already-firing daily probe, immune to all four relocation paths.

system_architecture.objects_touched: MODIFIED: scripts/anon-write-contract-probe.mjs (extend assertIngressBoundCannotBind), scripts/severity-pair-divergence-fence.mjs (unwire the coupling, drop the --json `count` key, delete extractLimitPredicate), lib/policy/severity-pair-coupling.js (delete compareCountVisibility, add the citations), tests/unit/severity-pair-coupling.test.js (remove its tests). NEW: probe-level tests for the equality. UNCHANGED: database/migrations/20260801_refresh_v_patterns_with_decay_column_drift.sql (chairman-verbal-bound; zero diff).
system_architecture.invariant: The anon-observed definer count equals the owner's true count. If they diverge, the rate limit no longer binds for some source_type and the ingress bound has silently stopped bounding.
system_architecture.coupling_map: live catalog + definer function -> anon-observed count vs owner true count -> equality assertion inside assertIngressBoundCannotBind -> the probe's existing daily exit code and reporting. The divergence fence loses one coupling and gains nothing.

implementation_approach.sequence: FR-5's citation first as a constraint (the SD description is already amended). Then FR-1/FR-2 — the equality in the armed probe, with TS-3's negative control written BEFORE the fire case, because the false positive is the thing most likely to be reintroduced. Then FR-4's retirement last, once the replacement demonstrably covers the re-inline path.
implementation_approach.verification_discipline: Seed the two failures that would make this look finished while being wrong: an unreadable basis reported as AGREES, and a build that still gates on relforcerowsecurity. Keep TS-1 as the positive control — a check that failed on every path would satisfy every negative scenario while alarming forever. Mutation-prove both directions; one direction plus an assumption is how the superseded design would have shipped.
implementation_approach.out_of_scope: Remediating v_patterns_with_decay's six missing columns (parent SD's remit, named as excluded-with-reason). Applying or editing the chairman-verbal-bound migration. Arming scripts/probe-anon-chairman-reach.mjs, which is dormant and watches a different function — worth its own item, not this one.

metadata.refutation_basis: postgres holds rolbypassrls; BYPASSRLS precedes the owner/FORCE test — proven by natural experiment on ai_gen_provenance and ai_gen_dwell_tracking
metadata.premise_proof: as anon: direct count 0, via definer fn 8, owner true count 8
